findings.premise: The design covers the original triage requirements and excludes upstream non-goals.
findings.evidence: The persisted LLD contains only the generic triageRationale 'feature tier (standalone LLD -> plan -> build).' Its referenced workflow run log contains step events, not the original params.storySpec or requirements. The analyzer returned an off-target bundle with empty upstream evidence. The inline ac1–ac8 statements therefore cannot independently establish upstream coverage. [files: .insrc/artifacts/LLD-f64ed70e71d2d5b7-S001.json, /Users/subhagho/.insrc/workflow-runs/f64ed70e71d2d5b7/design.story-wf-1793719881107-bhgwq2.jsonl]
findings.action: Attach or reference the original triage request/storySpec and map its requirements and non-goals to the contracts and acceptance tests.

findings.premise: Existing approval behaviour includes review enforcement, non-overridable BUILD freshness, write-once rangeBase, and clearing rejection on non-AMD approval.
findings.evidence: The approval function checks BUILD freshness before override handling, enforces review and other-party requirements, preserves an existing rangeBase, and executes 'delete nextMeta.rejectedAt' and 'delete nextMeta.rejectReason'. The code-review gate checks stale identity before its enforcement-off and override branches. [files: src/workflow/gates.ts, src/workflow/code-review/gate.ts]
findings.action: Retain these checks inside the proposed locked approval operation.

findings.premise: The references accurately distinguish existing behaviour from proposed implementation.
findings.evidence: Reference c16 says reads return readId, record reads and emit declared-read; handleArtifactContent currently performs read-only assembly and returns contentVersion without readId. Reference c36 says command-bar approval is migrated, but command.ts still calls 'const r = svc.workflow.approve(rest[0], true, override)' synchronously. Reference c34 says renderAmendment was added, but the markdown port currently returns null for kinds outside MD_KINDS, including AMD. [files: docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103f64ed70e/S001/LLD.md, src/workflow/artifact-content.ts, src/cli/command.ts, src/workflow/delivery/markdown.ts]
findings.action: Rewrite these references as verified baseline observations followed by proposed changes. Do not cite future behaviour as existing code evidence.

findings.premise: Content hashing and cross-process writer ownership have existing primitives suitable for extension.
findings.evidence: contentVersionOf hashes the full markdown with SHA-256 and returns its first 16 hex characters. withBuildWriter canonicalizes the artifact directory, acquires a create-only ownership file, refuses live contention, reclaims dead ownership under a takeover guard, and releases in finally. General artifact locking and a fresh-record callback would extend this existing BUILD-specific primitive. [files: src/workflow/artifact-content.ts, src/workflow/approval-owner.ts]
findings.action: Reuse these primitives while explicitly generalizing their scope and callback contract.

findings.premise: The per-host sequence fully contracts delivery of declared-read events and execution of decisions by the owning model session.
findings.evidence: The current socket server supports unary responses and request-scoped streams; the shared unary client closes its socket after a response. Chat presentation currently arrives through tool-call events carrying present declarations, and decideNow directly calls the review client. The LLD names an event and says 'owning session executes', but defines no host subscription/attachment contract, event delivery lifecycle, or correlated decision dispatch/result contract. It also leaves the cardinality and receiver selection of multiple host→model delegations unspecified. The persisted LLD supplies no sequence definitions or companions. [files: docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103f64ed70e/S001/LLD.md, .insrc/artifacts/LLD-f64ed70e71d2d5b7-S001.json, src/daemon/server.ts, src/shared/ipc-client.ts, src/mcp/daemon-stream.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/stream-events.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/chat-panel.ts, vscode-plugin/src/chat/docs-review-panel.ts]
findings.action: Contract the authenticated host event channel and owner-session decision request/reply, including attachment, delegation multiplicity, routing, disconnect/resume and inactive-owner handling. Document these relationships and the complete sequence in prose/tables or a generated companion, and include the affected stream/adapter contracts.

findings.premise: The FINAL writer inventory includes every production writer that can modify an artifact's JSON and markdown.
findings.evidence: The inventory omits migrate-docs-tree.ts. Its applyMetaRewrite reads artifact JSON and calls 'writeFileSync(rw.jsonPath, JSON.stringify(parsed, null, 2) ...)', then rewrites markdown labels. applyMigration also moves documents and rewrites links. The executable invokes applyMigration directly; neither it nor the executor establishes exclusion against daemon approval writers. These operations can race with the proposed locks and overwrite newly recorded presentation or approval state. [files: docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103f64ed70e/S001/LLD.md, src/workflow/migrate-docs-tree.ts, src/bin/insrc-migrate-docs.ts]
findings.action: Include migration writes and document moves in the concurrency contract. Specify compatible artifact locking or enforced exclusive maintenance, including rollback behaviour.

findings.premise: Keeping AMD as a virtual document preserves its existing storage shape, terminal transitions and attribution.
findings.evidence: AmendmentRecord stores status and approvedBy at the top level. approveAmendment preserves the supplied approvedBy and refuses any non-pending record. The pending scanner assigns AMD an empty mdPath, and the delivery markdown port excludes AMD. A virtual rendering avoids requiring a markdown-file migration. [files: src/workflow/amendments/types.ts, src/workflow/amendments/store.ts, src/workflow/pending.ts, src/workflow/delivery/markdown.ts]
findings.action: Keep the new renderer deterministic and preserve these flat fields and terminal transition rules.

findings.premise: The markerless non-AMD accept-or-repair policy defines an unambiguous canonical document compatible with existing records.
findings.evidence: Existing markdown has multiple composition paths: renderLldMarkdown renders the base artifact; reviewArtifactFile appends REVIEW_SECTION and renderReviewReport; question resolution appends renderResolvedQuestionsSection and renderCitationBlock. The LLD requires 're-render-matches' and repair, but does not define how these existing sections compose into canonical bytes or are preserved during repair. Using the base renderer alone would classify valid reviewed legacy documents as mismatches and could remove their displayed review on repair. [files: docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103f64ed70e/S001/LLD.md, src/workflow/artifacts/lld.ts, src/workflow/review/run-artifact.ts, src/workflow/questions.ts, src/daemon/steps/review-step/phases/verdicts.ts]
findings.action: Define canonical rendering per artifact kind, including review reports, question resolutions and other appended sections. Make publication, comparison and repair use that definition, with legacy reviewed/resolved fixtures proving preservation.

findings.premise: Stale BUILD review inputs remain detectable and cannot be bypassed through review overrides or disabled verdict enforcement.
findings.evidence: readStoredReviewFreshness distinguishes legacy, fresh and stale-review, including invalid or unavailable identity. enforceCodeReviewGate returns stale-review before evaluating enforcement or overrideReview. The direct BUILD approval boundary independently checks freshness, matching the invariant the design requires preserving. [files: src/workflow/code-review/input-fingerprint.ts, src/workflow/code-review/gate.ts, src/workflow/gates.ts]
findings.action: Keep freshness refusal independent of both requirePresent=false and review overrides.

findings.premise: Per-name presentation semantics handle multiple declared names resolving to the same artifact without returning superseded tokens.
findings.evidence: The existing present handler deduplicates name strings, not artifact identities. Its test deliberately presents one document by both 'LLD-ABC-S5' and its markdown path and expects both names in presented. The proposed recordPresentations returns tokens per recorded name and supersedes the previous token, but specifies no canonical-artifact grouping or conflicting-version policy. Minting independently for these accepted aliases would invalidate a token returned in the same successful response. [files: docs/standalone/enforce-approval-hard-gates-daemon-present-E20261103f64ed70e/S001/LLD.md, src/mcp/server.ts, src/mcp/__tests__/present-dispatch.test.ts]
findings.action: Resolve aliases before mutation, mint once per canonical artifact, and return the same token for equivalent declarations. Define refusal for conflicting alias versions/readIds and add this regression case.

findings.premise: Every declared inline acceptance criterion ac1–ac8 maps to planned tests supported by relevant existing harnesses.
findings.evidence: The acceptance table maps all eight criteria to unit, contract or integration scenarios. Existing present-dispatch tests exercise socket forwarding and response arrays; command tests use injectable Services; fingerprint tests cover semantic changes, exclusions and capture races; steering-refresh-through-daemon provides a child-process/socket isolation pattern. These support the proposed extensions. This verifies the test plan, not execution of the proposed tests. findings.action: Retain the mappings and add explicit cases for migration concurrency, canonical legacy section preservation, event-channel recovery and duplicate document aliases.

summary.prose: Enrolled-host trusted-display present-before-approve with a fully contracted per-host sequence: insrc_read emits a declared-read event that activates the panel; the enrolled host renders, acks with its capability proof, then present mints the token; tokens are delivered to the owning session and decisions execute there (delegation is host→model only, server-recorded). The TUI command-bar route migrates to the same async session-bound flow. AMD records use a virtual canonical rendered document — the canonical version is used for read/ack/present/approve and there is no markdown-agreement check for AMD. Approvals validate token+session+version under per-artifact locks and consume tokens; BUILD validates its sibling CR publication (CR lock first); publication is crash-safe; markerless legacy records accept-or-repair; rejected non-AMD reopens token-validated; AMD stays terminal; all writers inside the locked inventory; steering/guides update as one change with fail-closed legacy hosts.
